changes.title: OpenAI preservation order: deleted ChatGPT and API content kept for a court case
changes.summary: A US court ordered OpenAI on 13 May 2025 to preserve output log data that would otherwise be deleted, for the New York Times copyright case. OpenAI said this reached ChatGPT Free, Plus, Pro and Team (now Business) and the OpenAI API without Zero Data Retention. ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu, and API traffic under Zero Data Retention, were named as out of scope.
changes.action: Record the exposure from 13 May to 25 Sep 2025 in the vendor risk register for staff who used personal or Team ChatGPT for work and for API orgs without Zero Data Retention. No new action is needed for data created since 26 Sep 2025.

evidence.title: Order, The New York Times Company v. Microsoft Corporation, SDNY 1:23-cv-11195, ECF 551
evidence.quote: OpenAI is NOW DIRECTED to preserve and segregate all output log data that would otherwise be deleted on a going forward basis until further order of the Court

changes.title: Anthropic consumer terms: Claude chats may train models, with a choice due
changes.summary: Anthropic updated its consumer terms and privacy policy on 28 Aug 2025. Users on Claude Free, Pro and Max, including Claude Code on those accounts, must accept the terms and choose whether their chats are used to train models. With training on, new or resumed chats are kept for up to five years. Claude for Work (Team and Enterprise), Claude for Government, Claude for Education and API use, including Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI, are named as out of scope.
changes.action: Find staff using Claude Free, Pro or Max for work. Have them turn model training off, or move them to a Team or Enterprise plan.

changes.title: OpenAI lets API organisations restrict service tiers per project
changes.summary: OpenAI's API changelog entry of 21 Oct 2026 adds a control over service tiers. In the Platform settings an organisation can now limit the tiers each project is allowed to call, or set one limit at organisation level that applies to every project.
changes.action: Review the allowed service tiers in Platform settings if you want to limit cost or latency tiers across projects.

changes.title: GitHub makes GPT-6.1 Terra generally available in Copilot, enabled by default for Business and Enterprise
changes.summary: In a changelog post published on 26 Oct 2026, GitHub adds the GPT-6.1 Terra model to Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise. On Business and Enterprise an admin allows or blocks it in the Copilot model policy. New models are on by default, so it is live for an organisation unless an admin has switched off default enablement or blocked this model. Use is charged by usage at the model provider's list price. Copilot Free is not named. The page address carries 23 Oct, while the post's own published time is 26 Oct 2026 19:15 UTC, the date used here.
changes.action: If you keep an approved model list for Copilot, check the model policy now and disable GPT-6.1 Terra if it is not approved. If it stays on, check usage-based billing limits for the new model.

changes.title: Google turns request storage on by default for new Gemini API paid projects
changes.summary: Google's Gemini API changelog of 26 Oct 2026 says new projects using the Generate Content API on the paid tier now store requests by default (store=true). Existing projects keep their current setting. The note does not mention the free tier.
changes.action: Check any Gemini API project created from 26 Oct 2026. Set store=false per request or turn off Generate Content API logging in the Logs and Datasets settings if you do not want requests kept.

evidence.title: Gemini API changelog
evidence.quote: New projects using the Generate Content API (generateContent, streamGenerateContent, and batchGenerateContent) on the paid tier now store requests by default (store=true), matching the Interactions API.
